headline: Highest risk is AutoGen’s broad code-execution and filesystem/network access; the pair otherwise shows no documented direct interaction, so leakage/conflict/cascade risks are limited by B’s no-network profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can read/write files and run shell/subprocesses, so if spring-integration-samples is manually copied into its workspace, prompt-like content could influence execution. B has no documented ingestion path or shared channel, so the bridge is unusual and not default.
conditions: IF the operator copies B-generated text into AutoGen prompts or files
IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
mitigations: Keep separate workspaces for each agent
Disable copy-paste of agent outputs into prompts
Use read-only mounts for B artifacts
Add a human review step before any shell command
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen touches application data and can write/read the filesystem, while B is documented with no network egress and no touched data classes. Without a shared workspace or shared credentials, there is no clear default leakage path from B to external systems.
conditions: IF both agents share a filesystem containing sensitive application data
IF AutoGen is configured to send those files to a model provider
mitigations: Store sensitive files outside shared directories
Use local-only inference for AutoGen where possible
Restrict AutoGen workspace permissions
Rotate any exposed API keys
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data boundaries

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen has broad filesystem write and subprocess execution, while B is a runnable sample repository with no declared concurrency controls. If both are pointed at the same mutable workspace, write conflicts and state corruption are plausible even though B lacks write/network capabilities in its profile.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory
IF the operator runs B as a mutable local workspace alongside AutoGen
mitigations: Assign distinct working directories
Make B checkout read-only
Serialize any file edits through one agent
Avoid concurrent runs on the same repo
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen can generate code or instructions from application data, and B is a sample repository with no documented verification layer. If B consumes AutoGen output as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into incorrect travel-planning or sample-driven actions, though B has no direct action authority shown.
conditions: IF B treats AutoGen output as trusted input
IF no human or programmatic verification step checks AutoGen outputs
mitigations: Require explicit validation of AutoGen outputs
Add a second-pass reviewer
Limit AutoGen to draft-only mode
Log source provenance for every generated claim
requires-engineering: add schema validation before downstream use

E_compliance.rationale: AutoGen explicitly handles model-provider API keys and broad application data, while B’s profile is sparse and shows no residency or retention commitments. The main compliance issue is a potential policy mismatch if sensitive data is routed through AutoGen; B is not cited further because it exposes no relevant compliance surface.
conditions: IF sensitive or regulated data is passed into AutoGen
IF the operator relies on B for storage or retention guarantees
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to AutoGen
Review provider retention settings
Document data-flow boundaries
Use redacted test data
requires-engineering: obtain formal compliance review
